clue.text: Swearing in noughties President, take time out from exercising democracy

indicators.note: in means the president's letter is put inside what remains
take, paired with out from, tells the solver to remove the letter for time
take ... out from means the letter for time is removed from the voting word

parts.note: exercising democracy is casting a ballot, voting
George W Bush, president in the 2000s, was nicknamed Dubya after his middle initial W

explanation.surface: A political pundit grumbles about a president from the 2000s while urging people to skip voting.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a vow is swearing an oath, so the two participles are synonyms.

clue.text: Part of the elite, just like George

parts.note: just as in 'the very thing', meaning exactly
George Best was a famous Northern Irish footballer, so to be like George is to be Best

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be one of the elite, exactly as George is.
explanation.walkthrough: George Best was a celebrated Manchester United and Northern Ireland footballer of the 1960s and 70s.
explanation.definitionFit: The finest people in a group form its elite, so belonging to them is being among the top.

clue.text: Texan sows destruction, in a former manner of speaking

indicators.note: destruction smashes up the letters of the words texan sows so they can be rebuilt

explanation.surface: A Texan president spreads ruin, as people used to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sows destruction' reads as one phrase, but 'sows' is fodder and 'destruction' alone signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the Old English dialect of Wessex, an early tongue no longer spoken.

clue.text: Get Chilcot finally…cleared of all charges?

parts.note: to get a sum is to net it, as in earning a profit

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word Chilcot

explanation.surface: Will the Chilcot inquiry into the Iraq war end with someone acquitted?
explanation.walkthrough: The Chilcot inquiry was the British public inquiry into the Iraq war. 'Cleared of all charges' sounds legal but means after all deductions.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure after all deductions such as tax and fees is the take-home amount, punningly cleared of charges.

clue.text: Elect lab to manufacture insulin agent

indicators.note: to manufacture means to make something new out of the letters of elect lab

explanation.surface: Voters are urged to choose a laboratory that will produce insulin.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the pancreatic cells that produce and release insulin, so they are its agent.

clue.text: Doctor visits opera performing The Ring?

indicators.note: visits means the doctor's letters go inside the other letters
performing means the word opera is acted out in a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor goes to see Wagner's opera cycle, the Ring, being staged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Ring' looks like Wagner's operas but is a piece of jewellery for the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendant earring hangs from the lobe, so a ring worn there is an example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Jack Straw is "OTT, as bad as it gets"

indicators.note: to jack is to hijack or interfere with, so the letters of straw is ott are tampered with and reordered

explanation.surface: A quotation in which the Labour foreign secretary Jack Straw is called over the top and at rock bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Straw was Blair's foreign secretary during the Iraq war; his first name is the anagram signal, not part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for the lowest point or most extreme state that something reaches.

clue.text: President Erdogan holds the key

indicators.note: holds means the letters run inside the words President Erdogan

explanation.surface: The Turkish president is the one with the power to unlock things.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard key used to confirm a command or start a new line bears this name.

clue.text: 51-49 for Blair?

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
49 can be written as one less than fifty, IL, read here as one L

explanation.surface: A narrow 51 to 49 vote, the sort of result a prime minister like Tony Blair might win.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Tony Blair, but the answer is the first name of Lionel Blair, a British TV entertainer and dancer. 49 as IL means I (one) before L.
explanation.definitionFit: The forename of a well-known British dancer and television host who shared the surname Blair.

clue.text: Revise odds about 12 to upset United

indicators.note: about means the odds go around the other pieces

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the odds in betting
12 across is the president known as Dubya, from his middle initial W

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word to is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: A pundit reviews the odds on a president toppling a united front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' flips TO into OT.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise for an exam is to study hard, the student slang phrasal verb having that meaning.

clue.text: 12's haste to play the flip side of Give Peace a Chance?

definitions.text: 12's haste to play the flip side of Give Peace a Chance?

parts.words: 12's haste to play the flip side of Give Peace a Chance?
parts.note: the president's eagerness to do the opposite of John Lennon's anti-war song: haste is a rush, and the flip side of peace is war

explanation.surface: The president hurried to play the B-side of John Lennon's peace anthem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give Peace a Chance' is John Lennon's 1969 anti-war song; 'flip side' suggests a record's B-side but means the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for hurrying into armed conflict without exhausting diplomacy, the charge made against Bush over Iraq.

clue.text: Bars, at the outset, fertilisation technique not involving sex

indicators.note: not involving means the letters for sex are left out

parts.note: in vitro fertilisation, IVF, is a laboratory technique
sex is Latin for six, VI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A description of IVF as a way to conceive without intercourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sex' is the Latin word for six, so it gives VI.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening bars of a piece of music are its introduction, shortened in the familiar clipped form.

clue.text: Back-to-back winner to coach Hungary

parts.note: a coach is a bus
H is the international vehicle registration letter for Hungary

explanation.surface: A double champion is hired to train the Hungarian team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' looks like a verb but is a vehicle. The 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: George W Bush won the 2000 and 2004 presidential elections, two consecutive victories.

clue.text: Attacks drive a sudden rush

parts.note: to storm a place is to attack it
a drive is an urge or impulse

explanation.surface: Troops assaulting a position push on in one sudden rush.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal flood where the sea rises abruptly under a storm is a sudden rush of water.

clue.text: A dour lot, rebels in Islamic State are not true believers

indicators.note: in means the reworked letters sit inside the abbreviation

parts.note: IS is the abbreviation for the Islamic State group

indicators.note: rebels means the letters of a dour lot rise up and break their order

explanation.surface: Grim insurgents fighting within Islamic State are condemned as false believers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebels' looks like a noun but is a verb signalling the anagram of A DOUR LOT, giving DOLATROU.
explanation.definitionFit: Worshipping idols rather than the true god makes one a false believer; the adjective describes such people.

clue.text: Piers Morgan, for example, when in drink, made to look more attractive

indicators.note: when in means the former editor goes inside the word for drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink
Piers Morgan is a former tabloid editor, an ex-ed

explanation.surface: The broadcaster Piers Morgan, after a few drinks, looks rather better.
explanation.walkthrough: Piers Morgan edited the News of the World and Daily Mirror; the phrase recalls the 'sexed up' Iraq dossier.
explanation.definitionFit: To present something in a more exciting or appealing way is slang for jazzing it up.

clue.text: Customer for parlour Penny established in Dorset town

indicators.note: established in means the penny is set up inside the town's name

parts.note: Poole is a harbour town in Dorset, a county in southern England
D was the abbreviation for an old British penny, from Latin denarius

explanation.surface: A seaside shop is set up with a customer paying a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: The poodle was a jibe at Blair as Bush's lapdog.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog-grooming shops are called poodle parlours, so this dog is their typical client.

clue.text: I got stuck into rising tennis star, one likely to get seeded; failed horribly

indicators.note: got stuck into means the letter I is pushed inside the reversed name
rising in a down clue means the name reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: Rafael Nadal is a Spanish tennis champion
an egg is what gets fertilised

explanation.surface: A fan barges into a rising tennis player, a likely seed, who then loses badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns NADAL into LADAN. 'seeded' sounds like tennis rankings but means fertilised.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom, originally from theatre, for a performance or joke that flops completely.

clue.text: After High School dance, I observe one taking the pledge

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come later than the dance

parts.note: a prom is a formal American high-school dance
to observe is to see

explanation.surface: After the school prom, a teenager watches someone swear off drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking the pledge' suggests giving up alcohol but means receiving a promise.
explanation.definitionFit: In law the person to whom a promise is made is the receiver of that pledge.

clue.text: One casting movie director's unfinished Romeo

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the director's name is dropped

parts.note: Ang Lee is the Taiwanese-born director of Brokeback Mountain
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An actor in Ang Lee's incomplete film of Romeo is the one being cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casting' suggests film roles but means casting a fishing line.
explanation.definitionFit: A fisherman casts a line, so the definition describes someone fishing with rod and hook.

clue.text: Almost stab sailor; revolting, despicable individual

indicators.note: revolting means the whole string is turned over and read backwards
almost means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: to stab is to knife
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone nearly stabs a seaman, a disgusting, contemptible act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' seems to describe the person but turns KNIF plus TAR round.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for a contemptible person, especially an informer.

clue.text: In the Stasi, the DDR citizen is in the file

indicators.note: is in means the citizen goes inside the German article

parts.note: in German, as the Stasi would speak, 'the' is der
an Ossi is slang for an East German, a citizen of the DDR

explanation.surface: The East German secret police keep a citizen's record on file.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stasi was East Germany's secret police; the DDR was East Germany. The clue also nods to the Iraq 'dodgy dossier'.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection of documents on a person or subject is kept as a file.

clue.text: Motown's to lose Spielberg film rights

indicators.note: to lose means the film's letters are taken away

parts.note: Motown is the nickname of Detroit, so Motown's is Detroit's
E.T. is Steven Spielberg's 1982 film

explanation.surface: A Detroit record label loses the rights to a Spielberg movie.
explanation.walkthrough: Motown, a contraction of Motor Town, is Detroit, and also its record label.
explanation.definitionFit: French for rights, also used in English for legal dues and entitlements.

clue.text: Boring article about Congressman Brown

indicators.note: about means the brown colour wraps around the congressman

parts.note: tan is a shade of brown
REP is short for Representative, a member of Congress

explanation.surface: A dull newspaper piece about a congressman named Brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring article' sounds like a dull essay but is a tool for boring holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon's instrument for cutting holes in the skull is an article used for boring.

clue.text: Put in family member no longer left standing

indicators.note: in means the word put goes into the gap
no longer means the letter for left drops out

parts.note: a relation is a member of one's family

explanation.surface: Someone puts in a family member who is no longer upright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' seems to describe the relative but is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: One's standing is one's status or the esteem in which one is held.

clue.text: Managed to get doctor to turn out for accident

indicators.note: to get means the reversed doctor takes in the other piece
turn out means the doctor's letters are turned round

parts.note: GP, general practitioner, is a family doctor
to run something is to manage it, so managed is ran

explanation.surface: Someone managed to get a doctor to come out for an accident victim.
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is British slang for a minor car crash.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a crash, typically a minor collision in a car or aircraft.

clue.text: Handy place where one can get a date easily

definitions.text: Handy place where one can get a date easily

parts.words: Handy place where one can get a date easily
parts.note: the hand's inner surface is a handy place, and one variety of tree bears dates

explanation.surface: A tip for somewhere convenient to find a romantic partner.
explanation.definitionFit: It is part of the hand, hence handy, and the name of the tree that bears the date fruit.

clue.text: Stop regularly, as it seems

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words as it seems

explanation.surface: Someone appears to halt at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to stop or check it, as in stemming bleeding.

clue.text: Father introduced lecturer to Academy founder

indicators.note: introduced means the lecturer is brought inside the word for father

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A father presents a lecturer to the man who founded a college.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek philosopher who established the Academy in Athens around 387 BC.

clue.text: Nattiest dresser's last to go out like this!

definitions.text: Nattiest dresser's last to go out like this!

indicators.note: to go out suggests letters breaking ranks, so the pool is rearranged
last picks out the final letter of the word dresser

explanation.surface: The smartest dresser would be the very last to leave home in rags.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram 'to go out' uses NATTIEST plus R, the last letter of 'dresser'.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes in rags are torn to shreds, the state a smart dresser would never be seen in.

clue.text: Ask again about fat man's awful operation

indicators.note: about means the letters of ask again are moved around

explanation.surface: A doctor is asked again about an overweight patient's dreadful surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: Fat Man was the atomic bomb dropped on this Japanese city in 1945.
explanation.definitionFit: The city was the target of the Fat Man atomic bomb, a horrific military operation.

clue.text: One fleeing Iraq, perhaps after regime change

indicators.note: change means the letters of regime are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Refugees leave Iraq after the Saddam regime is toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regime change' reads as one political phrase, but 'change' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigrant, especially a political exile, has left their own country, of which Iraq is one example.
